background: Banco Santander is Spain's largest bank and one of the largest in the eurozone, run as a group of self-funded national subsidiaries across Spain, the UK, Brazil, Mexico, the US and elsewhere, with retail and commercial banking at its core.
synthesis: Ratings are strong at A+ on average across all three main agencies, all three on a stable outlook, with a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026 the latest move. Capital is the weak point against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 14.0% sits in the bottom quarter and leverage of 4.8% is under the peer median, though CET1 has risen 1.0 points since 30 Jun 2025. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 147% just below the peer median and NSFR of 124% at the median. The one flagged item, on 18 Sep 2026, is a strong quarter at the Chilean subsidiary; the group runs on lower capital than most of its peers but its ratings say the diversification earns that.
